prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (within 500 words)

Core purpose
- It’s time for change: end 14 years of Conservative chaos that has harmed family finances, public services and national security. Labour will restore hope through mission‑driven, fiscally responsible government that serves working people, partners with business and trade unions, and plans for the long term.

Foundations
- National security: unshakeable NATO commitment and UK nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review in year one; path to 2.5% of GDP on defence; tougher counter‑terror and counter‑state measures; “Martyn’s Law.”
- Secure borders: scrap Rwanda, create a Border Security Command using counter‑terror powers to smash smuggler gangs; new EU security agreement; clear the asylum backlog, end hotel use, expand returns; reduce net migration via a reformed points‑based system linked to skills and enforcement.
- Economic stability: iron fiscal rules (balance current budget; debt falling by year 5); one major fiscal event a year; strengthen the OBR; no return to austerity. No rises in National Insurance, Income Tax rates or VAT. Close non‑dom, private equity and offshore loopholes; modernise HMRC to tackle avoidance.

Five national missions
1) Kickstart growth
- Partner with business via a statutory Industrial Strategy Council; “securonomics” to crowd in private investment.
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to unlock 3:1 private capital in ports, gigafactories, steel, CCUS, green hydrogen.
- Cap corporation tax at 25% for the Parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates; one fiscal event a year.
- 10‑year infrastructure strategy; new National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; planning reform for homes, labs and energy; full gigabit and national 5G by 2030.
- Rail brought into public ownership as contracts expire; million potholes a year; EV charge‑point rollout; restore 2030 ICE phase‑out.
- Build 1.5m homes with restored housing targets, “brownfield first,” strategic “grey belt” releases, new towns, stronger affordable and social housing.
- Devolution in England with Local Growth Plans and multi‑year council settlements.
- New Deal for Working People: ban exploitative zero‑hours, end fire‑and‑rehire, day‑one rights, Single Enforcement Body, real Living Wage without age bands.

2) Clean energy superpower by 2030
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn), publicly owned, headquartered in Scotland, to co‑invest and drive local power.
- Double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; new nuclear (Hinkley/Sizewell/SMRs); strategic gas reserve; no new oil & gas licences; close windfall‑tax loopholes.
- Warm Homes Plan (£6.6bn) to upgrade 5m homes; carbon border adjustment; make UK the green finance capital; tough water regulation and nature recovery.

3) Take back our streets
- 13,000 extra neighbourhood police/PCSOs; Respect Orders; zero tolerance for shopworker assaults; halve knife crime in a decade; ban zombie knives/machetes; Young Futures hubs nationwide; specialist rape units and courts; tougher vetting and misconduct rules; fix prisons, cut reoffending.

4) Break down barriers to opportunity
- 6,500 new teachers; curriculum and assessment reform; free breakfast clubs in every primary; 3,000 school‑based nurseries; mental‑health professionals in every school.
- Skills England; transform FE into Technical Excellence Colleges; replace Apprenticeship Levy with a flexible Growth & Skills Levy.
- Fairness agenda: socio‑economic duty; Race Equality Act; disability and ethnicity pay‑gap reporting; full, trans‑inclusive ban on conversion practices; modernise gender recognition while upholding single‑sex protections.
- Housing security: abolish Section 21, raise standards, end leasehold for new flats and move to commonhold; action on homelessness.

5) NHS fit for the future
- Publicly owned, publicly funded. 40,000 extra weekly appointments (2m more a year); pooled waiting lists; use spare independent capacity; double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme.
- Return of the family doctor; more GPs; pharmacist prescribing; Neighbourhood Health Centres.
- Dentistry Rescue Plan (700,000 urgent appointments; reform contract).
- National Care Service with national standards and a Fair Pay Agreement.
- 8,500 extra mental health staff; Young Futures hubs; modernise the Mental Health Act.
- Prevention first: smoke‑free generation; curb junk‑food ads to kids; tackle vapes aimed at children; reduce stark health inequalities.

Politics in service of the country
- Independent Ethics and Integrity Commission; modernise Commons; immediate Lords reform (end hereditary peers, retirement at 80) and consult on full replacement; votes at 16; reset relations with devolved governments; remain in ECHR.
- Foreign policy: stand with Ukraine; AUKUS; clear‑eyed China strategy; make Brexit work (better EU trade, security pact—no single market/customs union/freedom of movement); targeted trade deals (incl. India); Clean Power Alliance; restore 0.7% aid when fiscal rules allow.

First steps for change
- Economic stability; 40,000 more NHS appointments weekly; Border Security Command; Great British Energy; crackdown on antisocial behaviour; recruit 6,500 teachers.
